minutes_text:
MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
  City Council, Community Development Financing Authority,
  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency,
  Housing Authority, and Library Board of Trustees*

  November 4, 2013

A Regular Meeting of the City Council, the Community Development Financing Authority, the
Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency, the Housing Authority, and the
Library Board of Trustees of the City of Mission Viejo, California, was called to order by Mayor
Reardon at 5:01 p.m., on November 4, 2013, at 200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo, California.

A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted
by 5:00 p.m. on October 30, 2013, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. Copies were also
posted at the Montanoso Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive, and the
Norman P. Murray Community and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.

*All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title "Council Member."

Present:  Council Member Leckness
  Council Member Schlicht
  Council Member Ury
  Mayor Pro Tem Kelley
  Mayor Reardon

Absent:  None

Staff Present:  Dennis Wilberg, City Manager
  William P. Curley III, City Attorney
  Keith Rattay, Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services
  Cheryl Dyas, Director of Administrative Services
  Karen Hamman, City Clerk

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Council Member Leckness

INVOCATION: Mayor Reardon

CLOSED SESSION

  CS1. Conference with Legal Counsel: Anticipated Litigation Initiation of Litigation
  Pursuant to Subdivision (c) of Section 54956.9: One Potential Case.

City Council Minutes  1  November 4, 2013
 RECESS TO CLOSED SESSION AND RECONVENE

At the hour of 5:03 p.m., Mayor Reardon recessed the meeting to Closed Session. The City
Council reconvened at 6:06 p.m. with all five City Council Members present.

REPORT OF CLOSED SESSION

City Attorney Bill Curley announced that the Council addressed one matter in closed session and
they voted to direct staff to proceed with the administrative enforcement of a contract. The vote
was 3-2 with Council Members Leckness and Schlicht dissenting.

PRESENTATIONS

P1.  Presentation on Veterans Day by Historian Bob Hayes

  Retired history teacher Bob Hayes discussed the history of Veterans Day and announced
  that the Community of Character theme for the month of November is thankfulness.

P2.  Presentation by Carl Hankey School on their International Baccalaureate Program

  The City Council received the presentation from Director of the IB program, Principal
  Diane Aguilera and IB coordinator Christine Grantz.

P3.  Business Recognition - Dr. Thomas E. Amen & Associates

  Mayor Reardon presented the proclamation to Dr. Thomas Amen and his wife, Owena.

P4.  Business Recognition - Mission Viejo Florist

  Mayor Reardon presented the proclamation to the owner of Mission Viejo Florist, Joni
  O’Neill.

P5.  Recognize the Mission Viejo Marine Adoption Committee

  Mayor Reardon with Colonel Joe Russell, Commanding Officer of Headquarters Battalion
  of the 1st Marine Division at Camp Pendleton, and 1st Sergeant Oscar Gomez presented
  certificates of appreciation to the members of the Marine adoption Committee.

P6.  Presentation on Wheelchair Tennis

  Hall of Fame wheelchair tennis player Karin Korb discussed the history of wheelchair
  tennis in Mission Viejo and reminded the audience that the 2013 NEC Wheelchair Tennis
City Council Minutes  2  November 4, 2013
   Masters (singles) will take place November 5-11, and the ITF Wheelchair Doubles Masters
  will be held November 7-11 at the Marguerite Tennis Pavilion.

PUBLIC COMMENTS

Gabbi Hammell, M.V.: asked the City to take a stand against animal cruelty and ban the use of
bull hooks for animal training.

Scott McKee, M.V.: announced that he placed a lattice extension atop the wall surrounding his
yard to keep his dog in. The extension was approved by the Oso Valley Greenbelt Architectural
Review Committee but subsequently disapproved by the Oso Valley Greenbelt Board of
Directors. Mr. McKee asked that the City to negate the decision of the HOA and allow him to
keep the wall as-is.

City Attorney Curley responded to questions from the Council Members and explained that the
City has no jurisdiction in the matter and therefore, will not be able to assist Mr. Mckee with the
problem.

David Verba, M.V.: expressed concern with speeding traffic along La Barca Road. He stated that
the street has become like an expressway and there have been 4 accidents in the last 2½
months. Mr. Verba asked that the City install a speed sensor along La Barca to monitor this
ongoing issue.

CONSENT CALENDAR

Item 5 was removed from the Consent Calendar for separate discussion.

Motion made by Council Member Ury, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Kelley, to approve the
Consent Calendar as described below.

On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, Schlicht, and Ury
NOES:  None
ABSENT:  None

1.  Waive Reading of Ordinances and Resolutions

  Approved the reading by title of all ordinances and resolutions and declared that said titles
  which appear on the public agenda shall be determined to have been read by title and
  further reading waived.

2.  City Council Minutes

  Continued to the next City Council Meeting.

City Council Minutes  3  November 4, 2013
 3.  Check Register Dated October 11, 2013 in the Amount of $295,739.00

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

4.  Check Register Dated October 18, 2013 in the Amount of $765,072.73

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

6.  Amending the Seven-Year Public Works Capital Improvement Program Beginning
  with the 2013-14 Fiscal Year to Recognize the Marguerite Parkway Stormwater and
  Transportation Runoff Abatement Project

  (1) Adopted Resolution 13-59 Authorizing the Director of Public Works to Apply for Funds
  for the Environmental Cleanup Tier 1 Grant Program Under Orange County Local
  Transportation Ordinance No. 3 for the Marguerite Parkway Stormwater and Transportation
  Runoff Abatement Project; (2) adopted Resolution 13-60 Amending a Seven-Year Public
  Works Capital Improvement Program Beginning with the 2013-14 Fiscal Year to Create
  Capital Improvement Project 220 to Include New Projects Relating to the Marguerite
  Parkway Stormwater and Transportation Runoff Abatement Project, Phase I (Via Florecer to
  Trabuco Road) and Phase II (Trabuco Road to Alicia Parkway) That Have Been Awarded or
  are Being Considered for Grant Funding Through the Orange County Transportation
  Authority Renewed Measure M2 Environmental Cleanup Program (ECP) in Accordance with
  Renewed Measure M2 Reporting Requirements; and (3) directed the Director of Public
  Works to transmit the amended Seven-Year Public Works Capital Improvement Program
  Beginning with the 2013-14 Fiscal Year to the Orange County Transportation Authority.

PUBLIC HEARINGS

OLD BUSINESS

7.  Mission Viejo Dog Park (CIP 313) Revenue Recognition and Budget Amendments

  Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services Keith Rattay presented the staff report.

  The following presented written comments in support of the recommended action: Dan
  Avery, M.V., Teri Gelbmann, M.V., and Carolyn "Cari" Cohn-Morros, M.V.

  The following presented written comments in opposition to the recommended action: Desi
  Kiss, M.V.

  Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Kelley, seconded by Council Member Ury, to (1) issue a
  change order to GMC Engineering in an amount not to exceed $198,000 and issue a
  purchase order and (2) adopt Resolution 13-61 Amending CIP 313 Mission Viejo Dog Park
  Budget by $190,600 for Bid Alternate Irrigation Installation and $21,834 to Recognize the
  Donations Received.

City Council Minutes  4  November 4, 2013
   On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, and Ury
  NOES:  Reardon and Schlicht
  ABSENT:  None

8.  CAL Card Audit Cost Proposal

  Cheryl Dyas, Director of Administrative Services, presented the staff report and answered
  questions of the City Council.

  Motion made by Council Member Ury, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Kelley, to direct staff
  to contract with Rogers, Anderson, Malody and Scott for an audit of the City's CAL Card
  program in the amount of $5,000.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

NEW BUSINESS

9.  Ordinances Adopting the 2013 California Fire and Building Codes

  Director of Community Development Chuck Wilson presented the staff report.

  Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Kelley, seconded by Council Member Ury, to (1)
  introduce Ordinance 13-300 Adopting by Reference the 2013 Editions of the California
  Building, Residential, Plumbing, Electrical, Mechanical, Green Building Standards,
  Historical Building, and Existing Building Codes, and the 2012 Editions of the
  International Swimming Pool and Spa Code and International Property Maintenance Code,
  Together, with Certain Appendices and Amendments Thereto, and Amending Title 8 of the
  Mission Viejo Municipal Code"; and (2) introduce Ordinance 13-301 Adopting by
  Reference the 2013 California Fire Code, Together with Certain Amendments and
  Deletions"; and (3) schedule a Public Hearing for December 2, 2013 to Adopt the
  Ordinances Identified in Items (1) and (2).

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

City Council Minutes  5  November 4, 2013
 10. Independent Accountant’s Report on Applying Agreed-Upon Procedures

  Director of Administrative Services Cheryl Dyas presented the staff report.

  The City Council received and filed the report.

11. Revisions to the City of Mission Viejo Flexible Benefit Plans and Fixed Monthly City
  Contribution Schedule and City of Mission Viejo Personnel Policies

  Director of Administrative Services Cheryl Dyas presented the staff report.

  Motion made by Council Member Ury, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Kelley, to (1) adopt
  Resolution 13-62 Providing for the Establishment of and Revisions to Personnel Policies;
  and (2) adopt Resolution 13-63 Revising the City's Flexible Benefit Plans and Fixed
  Monthly Contribution Schedule effective November 1, 2013.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

RECESS

At the hour of 8:38 p.m., Mayor Reardon declared a recess. The City Council reconvened at
8:46 p.m. with all five City Council Members present.

ITEMS REMOVED FROM THE CONSENT CALENDAR

5.  Ordinance Pertaining to Public Cost Recovery for Multiple Calls to Disruptive
  Gatherings

  The following presented written comments in opposition to the proposed Ordinance: Donna
  Bourassa, M.V. and Ed Sachs, M.V.

  Motion made by Council Member Ury, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Kelley, to adopt
  Ordinance 13-299 Adding Chapter 11.23 of Title 11 of the Mission Viejo Municipal Code
  Regarding Public Cost Recovery for Multiple Calls to Disruptive Gatherings.

  Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Kelley, seconded by Council Member Ury, to call for the
  vote and stop the debate.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

City Council Minutes  6  November 4, 2013
   AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, and Ury
  NOES:  Reardon and Schlicht
  ABSENT:  None

  On roll call, said MAIN motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, and Ury
  NOES:  Schlicht
  ABSENT:  None

MAYOR’S, COMMISSION, COMMITTEE REPORTS AND ACTIONS

12. Orange County Fire Authority (OCFA) Report

  Mayor Reardon read a written statement from resident Stephen Wontrobski regarding his
  belief that the City of Mission Viejo may be owed an equitable relief adjustment from the
  OCFA.

  Mayor Pro Tem Kelley presented the report.

13. Foothill/Eastern Transportation Corridor Agency Report

  Mayor Reardon announced that there has not been a recent meeting of the Foothill/Eastern
  TCA.

14. San Joaquin Hills Transportation Corridor Agency Report

  Mayor Reardon announced that there has not been a recent meeting of the San Joaquin
  Hills TCA.

15. Orange County Transportation Authority (OCTA)

  Council Member Ury presented the report and answered questions of the City Council.

16. Orange County Vector Control District

  Council Member Leckness stated that he had nothing to report.

STAFF REPORTS

City Council Minutes  7  November 4, 2013
 City Manager’s Report

17. Report on Recent Actions of the Successor Agency Oversight Board

  City Manager Wilberg presented the report.

Mr. Wilberg introduced Jonathan Pool who is a Masters candidate at Cal State Fullerton. The
Orange County City Manager’s Association has created a fellowship program to pair masters
students with cities and Jonathan was assigned to City Manager Wilberg. The two have attended
a number of workshops and meetings together and they will continue to do so through the
coming year.

City Attorney’s Report

City Attorney Curley announced that he will be working on an update of the Council's Rules of
Order policy which he plans to base on Rosenburg's Rules of Order.

COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS AND ACTIONS

18. Council Member Reports of Events and Activities Attended

  The City Council Members acknowledged their event and activities calendars as presented
  in the report and agreed to provide any changes to the City Clerk for the public record.

Council Member Leckness

Council Member Leckness stated that he had nothing to report.

Council Member Schlicht

19. Farmers Market

  Council Member Schlicht postponed this item to the next City Council meeting due to the
  lateness of the hour.

Council Member Schlicht outlined her attendance at the Ming for Supervisor fundraiser and the
Diablos' Mission for the Armed Forces football game. She stated that it was extremely moving to
be in a crowd of thousands who were very respectful of our service men and women. At the end
of the game, the football players took the jerseys off their backs and handed them to the
veterans. She stated that it was wonderful for the vets to be recognized for serving in multiple
wars and that she will always be grateful. Council Member Schlicht discussed the Drug Walk
and key note speaker David Wagner's moving story about the accident that paralyzed him. She
also announced that the Anaheim Ducks have applied for a permit for a skating rink in Mission
Viejo and that there is a new newspaper in town called Community Common Sense. Council
City Council Minutes  8  November 4, 2013
 Member Schlicht concluded her comments with a quote from Thomas Jefferson, "In questions of
power, then, let no more be heard of confidence in man, but bind him down from mischief by the
chains of the Constitution."

Council Member Ury

Council Member Ury thanked his colleagues for allowing him to miss the last meeting so he
could celebrate his 24th wedding anniversary with his wife. He announced that he had the
opportunity to MC an event on tourism for the Association of California Cities-OC. The meeting
was held at Movieland Wax Museum in Buena Park where Bodies... The Exhibition and Titanic
The Experience were on display. Council Member Ury stated that both exhibits were very
interesting and he encouraged residents to visit the museum.

Mayor Pro Tem Kelley

Mayor Pro Tem Kelley thanked City staff and the Saddleback Valley Unified School District
recreation department for putting on another fantastic Hometown Halloween. She attended the
event with 3 of her grandchildren and she noted that they had a fabulous time. Mayor Pro Tem
Kelley stated that this is just another unique thing that the City does to help make the community
special for the residents. She also provided a reminder that the wheelchair tennis events will be
coming up from November 5 through 11 and this is a very unique opportunity to have the
international event here in Mission Viejo, the first time in the United States. Mayor Pro Tem
Kelley also provided a reminder that the City will hold its annual Veterans Day ceremony on
November 11, 2013, at 2:00 p.m. and she encouraged residents to come out and honor veterans
and bring their children along so they will understand why we celebrate Veterans Day. She
further announced that the Mission Viejo Activities Committee Gifts and Goodies Boutique will
be held on November 16 from 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. Lastly, Mayor Pro Tem Kelley announced
that the Community of Character word for the month of November is thankfulness and she read
an excerpt on the benefits of being thankful from the Community of Character fliers which are
delivered to every school and classroom in Mission Viejo.

Mayor Reardon

Mayor Reardon discussed her attendance at the Mission for the Armed Forces football
game. She stated that it was phenomenal for the veterans to hear the students singing the
military hymns and to watch them create a human arch for the veterans to walk through as the
rest of the crowd shouted "U.S.A". Mayor Reardon noted that there were a lot of tears in the
veterans' eyes and it was an unbelievable sight. She read a note from resident and veteran Jerry
Silverstein who praised the City and the community for the outpouring of love and respect for its
veterans. Mayor Reardon announced that she attended the high school band competition at
Mission Viejo High School where Mission Viejo won third place in its division. She also
participated in tours of the South County Outreach and the new performing arts theater at
Capistrano Valley Highs School. She reminded residents that the Elks Club will honor veterans
on November 5 at 7:00 p.m.; the City will hold its annual Veterans Day ceremony at the Murray
Center at 2:00 p.m. on November 11th; and El Toro Memorial Park will hold a ceremony at 11:00
a.m. on Veterans Day as well. Mayor Reardon concluded her comments by asking her
City Council Minutes  9  November 4, 2013
 colleagues to pray for the family of Lake Forest Council Member Kathryn McCullough whose
husband and daughter are both hospitalized currently.

ADJOURNMENT

At the hour of 10:17 p.m., with no further business to come before the City Council at this
session, Mayor Reardon adjourned the meeting to Monday, November 18, 2013, at 5:00 p.m.

______________________________________________
Karen Hamman, City Clerk

Approved at the meeting of November 18, 2013

City Council Minutes  10  November 4, 2013
